label: Spawn phase (bass)
_note: Phase triggers are T2-sourced from water temperature during the warming half of the year (N. hemisphere: Feb-Jun). Outside that window — or inside the spawn band during the cooling half — no phase applies (null-safe). The rig-fit translations are T5 editorial and live only in the capped tie-break layer (kb/CONDITIONS.md); while a spawn phase is active it SUPERSEDES the month-based season fits, so the two never stack.

provenance.author: conditions-pass/1.0
provenance.note: trigger quotes T2 verbatim; rig-fit translations T5

citations.source: Take Me Fishing — Determining factors for freshwater fish spawning times (Mar 2018)
citations.quote: As an example, largemouth bass prefer water temperatures between 60-75 degrees for spawning, while bluegill spawn when water temperatures are in the 75-85-degree range.
They move closer to spawning areas as the water warms to about 55 degrees.
Largemouth bass move into shallow water to actively feed when the water temperature is 55 to 62 degrees and become more aggressive.

citations.claim: spawn focus / big females off feed
citations.source: Take Me Fishing — Largemouth bass spawning and fishing considerations (Feb 2016)
citations.quote: As water approaches about 55 degrees bass are focusing on spawning and the big females may not be in the mood to eat.
They guard the nest for 10 to 14 days while the eggs incubate and hatch.
After this recovery period until summer, females sometimes move out on the deeper edges and secondary points.

citations.source: Take Me Fishing — 5 pre-spawn bass fishing tips (Feb 2017)
citations.quote: An ideal spot before bass spawning season is a cove with an inlet and a shelf that drops off into deeper water.
